report.tagline: India's largest online marketplace, owned mostly by Walmart, selling phones, fashion, electronics and groceries to hundreds of millions of Indians, now also delivering in minutes.
report.simpleSummary: Flipkart is India's biggest shopping app. You can buy a phone, a TV, clothes or groceries, often with no-cost EMI and bank discounts. Its yearly Big Billion Days sale is one of India's biggest shopping events. It now also delivers daily items in about 10 to 15 minutes through Flipkart Minutes. Flipkart earns from seller commissions, delivery and platform fees, and ads.

overview.whatItDoes: Flipkart is a marketplace where lakhs of sellers list products and Flipkart handles search, payments and delivery through its logistics arm Ekart. It is strongest in mobiles, electronics and fashion (with Myntra), and is pushing into quick commerce (Flipkart Minutes), travel (Cleartrip), payments (super.money) and food delivery. Its edge is reach in small towns, cheap credit options and big sale events.
howItWorks: Shoppers browse in English, Hindi and other Indian languages, or use voice search.
Sellers list items and pay commission, fixed fees and shipping fees; Flipkart also adds a small platform fee per order for shoppers.
Ekart picks up from sellers and delivers to over 19,000 pin codes, including cash on delivery.
Bank offers, no-cost EMI and Flipkart Pay Later help people afford phones and TVs.
Big Billion Days and other sales bring huge spikes in orders and new users.
Flipkart Minutes delivers groceries and essentials from dark stores in about 10 to 15 minutes.
overview.valueProposition: For shoppers: wide choice, low prices and easy payment options, even in small towns. For sellers: access to crores of buyers and delivery to the whole country. For Flipkart: the default place Indians buy big-ticket items, which it can expand into daily needs.

businessModel.summary: Flipkart earns a cut and fees from sellers, delivery and platform fees from shoppers, and ads from brands. It is still losing money but narrowing losses.

revenueStreams.detail: Commission by category plus fixed and shipping fees.
Brands and sellers pay for top placement.
₹13,733 crore revenue in FY25, partly from outside clients.
Platform and handling fees per order, and delivery fees on small orders.
Myntra (₹548 crore profit FY25), Cleartrip, credit and payments.

businessModel.pricing: Free to shop; small platform fee per order and delivery fee below a minimum order. Seller commission varies by category, roughly 5% to 25%, with reported zero-commission schemes for low-priced items. Flipkart Black membership is a paid tier.
businessModel.unitEconomics: On a ₹15,000 phone, Flipkart might earn about ₹750 to ₹1,200 from commission and fees, plus some ad money, while spending ₹100 to ₹150 on delivery and payment costs. Fashion orders have higher commission but high returns, which can turn them into losses. Quick commerce orders of about ₹400 still lose money per order because dark stores and riders are costly until volume grows.

growth.moat: Flipkart's moat is its reach and logistics in small-town India plus deep partnerships with phone brands and banks. Ekart covers pin codes rivals still struggle with.

pmLessons: Design for the next user, not the current one: vernacular UX and EMIs opened small-town India.
Big events like Big Billion Days can win users, but trust breaks if orders get cancelled.
Incumbents must defend against new formats like quick commerce, even if it costs money.
Profit matters before an IPO: Walmart wants breakeven first.
